correctness.rationale: For every 0<a<1, 0<epsilon<1 and every integer n>=1: f_a integrates to 1 and yields a symmetric stationary circle-copula kernel. The uniform-mixture decomposition determines all lag kernels. Character Fourier action establishes rho(n)=(epsilon*r_a)^n and r_a in (0,1). The oscillatory-gamma estimate gives |fhat_a(k)| asymptotic to c(a)k^{-(1-a)} with a positive limiting real phase. Young yields bounded n-fold density when n(1-a)>1; Fejér means diverge when n(1-a)<=1, including odd lags and equality. Even-lag positive Fourier coefficients give the exact relative coefficient; uniform Fourier remainder bounds yield the critical simple pole. Rational and numerical consistency tests in CHECK.py passed. All singular boundary cases and unproved generalizations are explicitly excluded.

value.rationale: Exact first finite psi lag is a natural, previously unspecified analytic invariant for stationary copula Markov kernels, measuring worst-case conditional event amplification rather than merely covariance. A complete parameter/lag classification for the natural integrable power-cusp family reveals arbitrarily long infinite-psi plateaus with a fixed Doeblin minorization and arbitrarily small maximal correlation. Explicit even-lag series and critical poles describe the transition, with relevance to dependent-data risk and mixing-based inference. This is structural behavior, not a routine finite table or mere renaming.
